gnosh ssh

  Run ssh, putting what the far side copies on this machine's clipboard. Every
  word after ssh is ssh's (but for -h or --help alone, which shows this), and
  gnosh ssh ends with ssh's status. At a terminal, ssh keeps the terminal, its
  passwords and its job, and what it writes passes through gnosh as it is,
  which puts the text of each copy the far side makes through the terminal
  (OSC 52: gnosh's /copy, tmux's copy mode) on this machine's clipboard as
  well. Apple's Terminal drops such copies, so there a shell function can send
  each interactive ssh through gnosh ssh. Without a terminal, where this
  machine has no clipboard tool (pbcopy, wl-copy, xclip, xsel), or with -f,
  gnosh ssh is plain ssh.

  Not built yet in this build of gnosh: typing it stops with a message that
  says so.

Usage
  gnosh ssh [flags] [ssh arguments...]

Flags
  -h, --help
      Show help: gnosh's, or after a command's name that command's.
